title: Monthly Report ownership and carryover: current mechanisms and decision record
purpose: Review artifact only, not runtime configuration: it does not authorize policy changes, migration, data promotion or deployment.

status_definitions.explicit_requirement: A cited owner intake explicitly requires the narrow rule described by decision_sources.supports; other row details are not thereby approved.
status_definitions.meeting_intent: The intake requests reuse, but does not settle every authority, identity, status or promotion choice.
status_definitions.existing_implementation: A current-code mechanism at audited_main. This is not blanket business-policy approval or served acceptance.
status_definitions.proposed_policy: A proposed boundary for owner review; not an implemented action or authorization to write shared data.
status_definitions.open_decision: A broader business choice remains unresolved. Preserve the separately described current mechanism.

scope_definitions.organization: The existing shared ENFRA branding catalog; this does not make contract workflows or client data universal.
scope_definitions.contract: One canonical contract identity; client-logo reuse additionally requires its explicit catalog mapping.
scope_definitions.contract_site: One contract with explicit site membership, site rows or single-site overrides; no inferred cross-contract membership.
scope_definitions.report: One working report and its separately saved contract/profile/month revisions; a snapshot is not approval.
scope_definitions.report_month: Facts and output belonging to a report period; original evidence may remain as historical context.
scope_definitions.source_archive: Retained original bytes and receipts, distinct from report inclusion or approval; existing shared-reference audiences are unchanged.
scope_definitions.unresolved: No broader ownership rule has been approved by this record; the current selected-site mechanism remains in force.

global_safety_invariants: This JSON is review data, not runtime configuration, policy signoff, a migration command or release approval.
Saving a report snapshot preserves work, including unreviewed work; it does not establish source, artwork or output approval.
Standing revisions and report revisions are separate. Existing locks, expected-revision checks and historical versions remain applicable.
Current qualified directory edits, safe capacity first fill and explicit Training matrix edits can write shared records; do not invent a universal extra Save shared version gate.

Contract A workflow and site data do not become contract B defaults. Client-logo reuse requires an explicit mapping for the target contract: an A-only mapping does not authorize B, while one catalog entry may explicitly list both. The shared ENFRA logo is a separate organization-level mechanism.

Report omission is not deletion of original bytes or published history. Starting Report Omit-reversal repair #687 is merged; its scope is review/edit retention, not authorization to delete originals or history.
Clearing current-month output during rollover does not imply deleting stored originals, retained source context or earlier saved reports.
Legacy workflow artifact adoption does not reconstruct missing historical source-page approval; preserve that limitation.
Source storage, reference-shelf download and content approval are different acts; existing privacy and audience controls remain unchanged.
Document/schema tests and synthetic mechanism tests are not native-browser, genuine Word/PDF, deployment or owner acceptance.

items.label: ENFRA brand logo / approved company identity
items.source: Reviewed ENFRA entry in the shared logo catalog; report copies are pinned.
items.notes: The existing organization-level ENFRA logo is distinct from contract workflow diagrams and contract-mapped client logos.
items.report_override: A report's custom or omitted logo is not replaced by ordinary defaults; changing it does not edit the catalog.

current_mechanism.summary: The versioned branding catalog is shared. find_logo selects the explicit enfra entry for the company logo, while apply_defaults fills only an eligible empty brand_logo slot and preserves populated, omitted and caller-protected slots. Saving the catalog requires a named, confirmed actor and its current revision. Reports keep selected image bytes/references; catalog replacement does not rewrite their saved history.
limitations: The meeting intake does not define a new publishing-role model. This record neither expands catalog access nor generalizes its global scope to report content.

decision_sources.supports: Requests an ownership/carryover decision record; does not approve every proposed rule or authorize migration.

open_choices: Any new organizational publishing authority or cross-organization branding policy needs a separate decision; current named/confirmed writes remain unchanged.

items.label: Client logo and contract terminology
items.source: Explicit client-contract mapping in the shared logo catalog, copied into the report.
items.notes: Catalog storage is shared, but client-logo selection requires explicit membership for the target contract. One entry may list several contracts; an A-only mapping does not authorize B. Matching names or images do not create a mapping.
items.report_override: A populated or omitted report logo remains pinned; an explicit report replacement does not publish a new catalog mapping.

current_mechanism.summary: find_logo selects a client logo only when the report contract is listed in that catalog entry. apply_defaults fills an eligible empty client_logo slot, verifies its bytes and reuses the saved artwork review; it does not approve an already pinned custom image. Catalog changes use a separate confirmed revisioned save, and old report snapshots retain their selected copies.
limitations: An existing code mapping is not evidence that a different client or contract has authorized that artwork.

decision_sources.supports: Requests an ownership/carryover decision record; does not approve every proposed rule or authorize migration.

items.label: Report cover photograph
items.source: Selected cover_photo block and retained original/asset reference in the report.
items.notes: A photograph is not a logo. Retaining a prior photo does not establish that it depicts newly completed work.
items.report_override: Use or omit a photograph for this report; leave catalog logos, installed design and historical versions unchanged.

current_mechanism.summary: The ordinary Change cover photograph flow changes the report's photo slot. Replacement preserves review only when the exact selected artwork remains unchanged; a new choice receives its own review state. No cover photograph sets source to Omit while retaining its asset references. Rollover retains the non-monthly photo block; it does not publish a shared photo master or rewrite earlier report versions.
limitations: The separate Starting Report Omit/reinclude text-table repair in #687 is unmerged at this baseline; this photo behavior does not prove that broader repair.

items.label: Business-hours outage workflow diagram
items.source: Versioned procedure pictures explicitly published for the canonical contract.
items.notes: Contract isolation is an explicit requirement. Current code implements it; legacy global records are read-only adoption candidates, not active global defaults.
items.report_override: Keep populated or omitted report pages; explicit Use replaces procedure pictures while retaining adjacent notes and tables.

current_mechanism.summary: Current workflow standards are contract-scoped. Publishing checks the current report block, its fingerprint, reviewed pictures, source-page/site admission and the expected standing revision. Defaults fill only eligible blank included slots; the guided loader suppresses this default path for saved, recovered and rolled-forward reports. Explicit Use replaces pictures while preserving adjacent notes/tables. Legacy adoption requires matching recorded origin contract, an exact review receipt and a recheck under lock; adoption alone does not replace current report pages.
limitations: The narrow independent-artifact legacy route does not recover missing original source-page history or validate that lost approval. Current UI states this limitation.
Default availability for a new report is different from automatically replacing the pinned procedure of a carried or reopened report.

items.label: Organizational chart / site structure
items.source: Versioned contract chart default with optional explicitly published single-site overrides.
items.notes: Current implementation already supports contract defaults and single-site overrides. A combined-site report does not guess one site's chart.
items.report_override: Explicit report use preserves adjacent notes/tables; report edits do not publish a chart until the separate confirmed action.

current_mechanism.summary: Chart defaults already have a contract store, immutable revisions and optional single-site overrides. selected_default prefers the selected site's override, then the contract default; a multi-site report uses only the contract fallback. Publication requires an exact current chart, confirmed actor, scope, source-page/artwork review and expected revision. Defaulting preserves authored, omitted and excluded copies, with a narrow exception for a just-copied profile fallback. The guided loader suppresses defaults for saved, recovered and carried reports; an eligible empty imported block can still receive a default, but an imported populated chart does not receive the profile-fallback exception.
limitations: This is an implemented scope mechanism, not permission to infer a particular chart's contract-wide suitability from its filename or appearance.

decision_sources.supports: Requests an ownership/carryover decision record; does not approve every proposed rule or authorize migration.
Requires organization/workflow uploads to retain their intended contract/site scope.

items.label: Facility contacts and contract contact directory
items.source: Contract directory with contract-wide contacts and explicit site records; separate report copies.
items.notes: Do not apply subcontractor promotion rules to this existing facility-directory mechanism. Saved report history stays distinct from refreshed working copies.
items.report_override: Manual/unproved tables and removals stay report-only; qualifying verified Library edits may also update only their bound directory sites.

current_mechanism.summary: Directory defaults reuse known contacts for exact selected-site bindings when the named editor and empty-copy guards allow it. automatically_keep_directory_contact_edits can persist a narrowly verified Library-copy edit without another shared-save button: it checks historical rows/bindings, excludes contract-wide rewrites and ordinary additions/removals/reorders, and rejects same-site conflicts while preserving other sites. Explicit add intent has separate checks. refresh_directory_contacts can update an unchanged working copy from newer standing records; it does not rewrite historical snapshot bytes.
limitations: Not every contact edit is report-only, and not every edit qualifies for automatic keeping. Contract-wide contact administration remains a separate directory action.
Current direct-contact shortcut #693 and literal-label rendering #691 are separate unmerged changes; neither is required to describe these existing persistence rules.

items.label: Thermal capacity: site, plant and service values
items.source: Current contract capacity history contains source-bound rows with explicit site_keys.
items.notes: The unresolved decision concerns broader capacity-sharing authority, not a new prohibition on existing safe first fill. Preserve site, plant/service, units, NR, blanks and zero.
items.report_override: Existing manual/Omit report blocks stay pinned; an empty non-Omit block or unchanged pinned copy can refresh after a shared update.

current_mechanism.summary: Capacity already uses contract storage with explicit row-level site_keys and revisioned history. Safe first-fill rows can be persisted automatically when the existing UI has resolved site matches, a named actor, no unverified image and no duplicate identity; browsing alone is not a save. Corrections to existing reusable values require the existing reviewed update action. capacity_block filters rows to selected sites, resolve_capacity fills only empty non-Omit content, and can_refresh_capacity permits an empty non-Omit block or an unchanged pinned copy.
limitations: This record does not authorize copying A1 numerical assumptions to A2 or changing current first-fill/correction behavior.
The default/promotion policy cells describe the unresolved broader sharing decision; the current-mechanism paragraph states what the existing UI actually does.

decision_sources.supports: Requests an ownership/carryover decision record; does not approve every proposed rule or authorize migration.
Explicitly permits unambiguous first fill at its proper scope, with conflict-aware updates and zero browsing/layout writes.

open_choices: For each contract, decide whether any capacity assumption may apply to multiple sites and who can approve that applicability; retain current exact site partitions until resolved.

items.label: Subcontractor contacts, trade bands and contact instructions
items.source: Explicit, versioned contract-scoped approved subcontractor roster; ordinary report/profile contact tables remain distinct.
items.notes: Approved roster versions can be shared for explicitly eligible contract sites, not inferred across contracts. Report-only edits and source-page imagery never silently publish. Facility-directory automatic keeping remains a separate mechanism.
items.report_override: Report-only edits, exclusions and imported pages never update the approved roster; an explicit, revision-checked publication or Use action is required.

current_mechanism.summary: The merged #686 contract-scoped roster provides an independently versioned contract store with explicit reviewed-row publication, site validation, revision guards and a report-scoped Use action. The ordinary report contact editor, imported grouped trades, untouched original pages and saved report history remain separate. Shared roster application never silently edits an existing report or moves source-page approvals.
limitations: Contract-scoped roster APIs and report UI are merged, but genuine served/published acceptance remains separate; import alone is never roster approval.
Site scope and contract-wide status are explicit reviewer decisions. No historical report, page receipt or original source bytes are migrated to the roster.

decision_sources.supports: Requests an ownership/carryover decision record; does not approve every proposed rule or authorize migration.

items.label: Subcontractor status / when to contact
items.source: Report agreement/status cells and optionally approved site-eligible contract roster rows; no automatic effective-date inference.
items.notes: Preserve unknown, blank, false and explicit MSA/agreement states. Merged roster reuse can retain reviewed status cells for selected sites but does not establish current-month service completion or effective dates.
items.report_override: A report-only status correction does not republish the approved roster or create a new service event; explicit roster review/save is separate.

limitations: Existing scoped roster status reuse is explicit; effective/last-confirmed date policy and live served review remain open, not silently approved by this record.

items.label: Priority capital renewal recommendations
items.source: Report/profile Capital rows plus merged #684 versioned contract-approved master API and explicit site-selected occurrences.
items.notes: The #544 Capital replay guard and #687 Starting Report omission correction are merged. #684 adds an independently versioned, explicitly approved Capital master API with site overrides and financial controls, but does not by itself supply an ordinary report editor approval/reuse UI.
items.report_override: Report-only correction/omission and replay guards remain authoritative; master revisions never overwrite report choices or historical snapshots.

items.label: Pending and declined proposal items
items.source: Report proposal cards/tables with source occurrence, recorded decision and carried period.
items.notes: Pending, Declined, unknown and deliberately omitted are different states. Source or scope wording alone does not decide status.
items.report_override: Saved explicit decisions and report omissions remain attributable to that report; they do not publish a shared contract status.

current_mechanism.summary: Proposal normalization and carryover use source table decisions, existing row identities and saved manual choices. seed_followups retains included proposal context, distinguishes Pending from Declined and avoids treating a manually edited scope phrase as a new status. Report saves use their own revision/history. There is no separate standing proposal-status master in this path; a carried proposal remains historical context rather than a new-month event.
limitations: Omission from one report is not a contract decision to decline or permanently delete the proposal. Existing pricing and source-review gates still apply.

items.label: Open equipment issues and evidence/update status
items.source: Canonical report issues/followups and their source/evidence references.
items.notes: Unresolved issues and evidence can persist as history. Neither old evidence nor a carried status proves new work this month.
items.report_override: Report visibility/Clear and resolution are distinct; a fresh Updated claim requires the existing current-period confirmation.

current_mechanism.summary: canonical_issues reconciles report issue cards and followups; rollover retains unresolved issue context and its backing evidence. seed_followups applies its existing next-month inclusion rules and clears review state, while current-period confirmation gates a carried Updated claim. Therefore an issue omitted in one report is not necessarily permanently suppressed in future months, and report-only Clear is not resolution. Earlier saved report versions remain unchanged.
limitations: Do not promise that every omission persists identically through every future issue rollover; the documented current seed rules and resolution state determine that behavior.

items.label: Standing staff training requirements / annual status matrix
items.source: Versioned contract/year/site requirements registry, plus each report's pinned matrix reference.
items.notes: Annual matrix year identity is explicit. #715 joins cross-site requirement columns only by normalized case/whitespace identity, preserving per-site status, original column spelling and site scope; #762 captures delivered grid edits before Add requirement changes the schema.
items.report_override: A pinned matrix survives rollover; requirements-grid edits/Add requirement/Start YEAR write shared requirements, unlike report-only notes and sessions.

current_mechanism.summary: Annual matrices use training:matrix:v2:YYYY; legacy training:matrix:v1 remains year-unrecorded. Fresh reports seed exact-year selected-site rows or safely reset earlier statuses. #715 validates each site's requirement heading identity and combines equal case/whitespace titles without merging different people/sites or losing statuses; a pinned report retains its selected year. Requirements grid/Add requirement/explicit Start YEAR write selected-site/year standing data under revision checks, and #762 captures pending grid changes before adding a new requirement. Monthly notes and sessions remain report-only; no universal extra shared-Save step exists.
limitations: #715's normalized heading identity does not authorize punctuation-based aliases or guessed cross-site statuses; ambiguous duplicate headings are rejected.
#762's Add requirement input capture preserves delivered edits but does not auto-approve imported evidence or substitute for served/browser verification.

items.label: Completed training sessions (date, topic, participants, hours)
items.source: Report-bound training:events:v1 rows with dates, participants and hours.
items.notes: Completed requirements are not dated sessions. Merged #734 checks explicit source Training event-site columns in both new and restored reviews; ambiguous, foreign and duplicate-heading sites require manual correction or omission rather than silent cross-site inclusion.

A current-year training requirement status does not create a session.

items.label: Current-month work orders, service calls and operational narrative
items.source: Accepted report source rows/manual work with selected-site and period context.
items.notes: Current-month completion, PM/non-PM counts and zero require their existing evidence/coverage rules, not merely a repeated table.
items.report_override: Corrections and source selections belong to the working report and its saved versions; no automatic standing work-order publication.

current_mechanism.summary: CMMS mapping uses explicit selected sites, date/status interpretation and declared coverage; it retains evidence rather than inventing completion or zero counts. Source contribution receipts bind accepted uses to report/site/period facts. new_month_draft clears period-specific output rows while retaining source records still referenced by carried content. It does not publish a reusable current-work master or erase prior snapshots.

items.label: Scorecards, commissioning, water, vendor, progress photos and other attachments
items.source: Selected section/source-page occurrences and reviewed report asset copies.
items.notes: A page belongs to its reviewed source occurrence and destination. Current review, scope, privacy and resource gates remain applicable.
items.report_override: Page inclusion/caption/Omit changes report output; it does not delete an original or publish it as standing content.

current_mechanism.summary: prepare_section_pages validates explicit selected pages and destination ownership against current report content, preserves page provenance and applies the existing page-review and size limits. new_month_draft removes period-specific attachment output; issue/proposal evidence and other referenced source context can remain under their own carry rules. Saved report versions and source originals are separate from the new month's selected pages.
limitations: The separately owned equipment gallery #690 and PDF preparation #669 are not claimed as merged by this record.
Blank or cleared monthly output does not imply that all source metadata or archived bytes disappeared.

items.label: Imported report, uploaded source file and shared reference shelf
items.source: Hash-verified stored originals and receipts; separate report references and shared reference shelves.
items.notes: Reference storage is not report approval, tenant ownership assignment or authorization to promote/import content.
items.report_override: A new replacement has its own identity/review; a report reference or omission never edits bytes under an old source identity.

current_mechanism.summary: ingest stores source bytes under the existing profile/contract namespace and records their digest; source_bytes verifies the selected original before use. Saved report references and reviews are separate from those bytes. The shared reference-bundle shelf is a distinct immutable, discoverable no-login testing facility with its existing audience; its user-supplied manifest is not approval to import, adopt a standing default or assign an acceptance scenario. Rollover retains only source records still referenced by carried content and does not perform an archive migration.
limitations: The source shelf is not a newly permissioned private vault; this document adds no authentication or access policy.
Original preservation does not imply every temporary QA lease is permanent; existing fixture retention and quotas remain unchanged.
